title: Retention that runs itself
brief: 17:15. The old finance share is full. IT asks you to decide what goes before they move it, record type by record type.
role: Accounts payable, owner of the old finance share
insight: Keeping everything feels safe. It is the opposite: every old record is one more thing to lose in a breach.
teaches: Keep records as long as a law or a real need says, and no longer
A retention schedule turns “should we delete this?” into a rule that runs itself
Delete, or anonymise what you want to keep for statistics

value.title: Clear out the old finance share before the move
body: “We are moving the old finance share on Saturday. Can you mark what we delete and what we move? Everything on it is below.”

head: Folder
What it holds
Oldest
rows: CVs from people who applied and were not hired
Pay records of staff who left in 2023
Customer chats with names and addresses

policy.title: Veltrix retention schedule (extract)
lines: Financial records (invoices, payments, payroll): 6 years from the end of the financial year, for tax and company law.
Unsuccessful job applicants: 6 months after the decision.
Customer support records: 2 years. Anonymised statistics may be kept.

options.label: Delete: past the 6 years
options.why: The legal reason to keep them has run out.

options.label: Keep, just in case
options.why: “Just in case” is the risk. Past 6 years there is no reason to hold them.

options.label: Delete
options.why: Six months after the decision was years ago.

options.label: Keep, we might hire them one day
options.why: People's CVs, kept for years without their knowledge or a reason.

options.label: Keep until 2030, then delete
options.why: Payroll is a financial record: 6 years.

options.label: Delete, they have left
options.why: Leaving does not end the legal requirement.

options.label: Keep counts and themes only, with names and addresses removed
options.why: Anonymised statistics are no longer personal data.

options.label: Move them all as they are
options.why: Six year old chats with names and addresses, for no purpose.

choices.label: What do we keep from the old finance share?

script.say: Follow the schedule. Financial records six years, rejected applicants six months, support two years. Anything past that goes. Keeping it all is how a small breach becomes a big one.

setup.title: Work queue
setup.body: IT need a clear out list for the old finance share

outcome.label: Checked with data protection
outcome.what: The schedule decides, not a feeling.

outcome.label: Let the old CVs go
outcome.what: Personal data about people who never worked here, held for years. The easiest thing to forget, and to lose.
outcome.ideal: deletes data whose purpose has ended.

decide.objective: Mark what to keep and what to delete on the old finance share.
decide.insight: Use the schedule: keep for as long as a law or a real purpose says, then delete.

hint.text: Open the Work queue and read the retention schedule. Delete the 2017 invoices, the 2019 CVs and the old chats (or keep anonymised counts). Keep the 2022 invoices and the 2023 payroll. Then send the list.

outcome.label: Kept what the law needs, cleared the rest
outcome.what: Six years of invoices and payroll move; old CVs, chats and expired invoices are gone.
outcome.ideal: applies the retention schedule record by record.

card.title: Less to lose
body: Everything you had no reason to keep is gone before the move, so it can never leak. What the law needs moves, with a date to delete it.
Written into a schedule, this happens automatically every year, and nobody has to feel brave about deleting.
card.ideal: keeps data only as long as the schedule says.

outcome.label: Deleted records the law requires
outcome.what: Invoices or payroll records still inside the 6 years are gone. That is a tax and company law problem.

card.title: Gone too soon
body: The 2022 invoices and 2023 payroll records had to be kept for six years. A retention schedule works both ways: it says when to delete, and when not to.
card.ideal: keeps what the law requires, and deletes the rest.

outcome.label: Kept more than the schedule allows
outcome.what: Old CVs, chats or invoices with no reason to exist are moving to the new share, and will sit there for years.
outcome.ideal: treats keeping everything as the risk it is.

card.title: Keeping everything is the risk
body: Data you do not need can still be stolen, still has to be found for access requests, and still counts in a breach. Open the case to see which records should have gone.
card.ideal: deletes data whose purpose has ended.
